summary: Full backend + frontend testing of new Rubric Library feature (iteration 36). BACKEND (16/16 pytest cases PASS via /app/backend/tests/test_rubric_library.py): (a) GET /api/rubrics returns list with per-item can_edit flag (true for creator + super_admin, false otherwise) and 401/403 without token; (b) POST /api/rubrics creates rubric, returns rubric_id + can_edit=true, persists (GET reflects) — missing name -> 400, missing content -> 400, missing name field entirely -> 400/422; (c) PUT /api/rubrics/{id}: creator OK + updated_at advances forward (verified with 1.1s sleep), non-creator instructor -> 403, super_admin on other-user rubric -> 200, unknown id -> 404; (d) DELETE /api/rubrics/{id}: creator OK + no longer in GET list, non-creator -> 403 (still listed), unknown -> 404, super_admin on other-user rubric -> 200; (e) can_edit flag correctness verified across 3 personas (creator=true, other=false, admin=true) for the SAME rubric; (f) REGRESSION: feedback_template still works — POST /api/cohorts/{id}/materials with feedback_template persists on homework; PUT /api/materials/{id}/feedback-template updates + clears back to empty. Pre-existing test_feedback_template.py 16/16 also RE-VERIFIED PASS (no regression from Rubric route additions). FRONTEND (Playwright + super_admin session + ephemeral 2nd instructor for ACL): (1) /rubrics page loads for instructor + super_admin, empty state shows Create button + dialog opens; (2) Create -> card renders with 'Steven Lewis' creator label + persists across reload; (3) Edit via pencil updates card content in place; (4) Delete via trash + native confirm -> card disappears + 'Rubric deleted' toast; (5) NEW second-instructor session sees admin-owned rubric card but edit-rubric-{id} + delete-rubric-{id} testids ARE ABSENT (can_edit=false honored); own rubric icons ARE present; (6) Sidebar rubrics-link (data-testid=rubrics-link, href=/rubrics) visible on /dashboard; (7) Cohort UploadMaterialDialog: feedback-template-wrapper HIDDEN when material_type=workbook, and VISIBLE with picker-trigger + input + save-as-btn when switched to homework; picker option list includes existing rubrics; selecting rubric prefills textarea (43 char length from picked 'Custom AI instructions from library dialog.'); (8) Library UploadMaterialDialog exposes same field with lib-feedback-template prefix; Save-as flow: open save dialog -> fill name -> Save Rubric -> success toast + save dialog closes + new rubric appears in picker options; (9) MaterialsTab in cohort: Sparkles/Add-AI-Instructions click on homework card opens edit-feedback-template-dialog (NOT window.prompt — verified via dialog listener with 0 hits); Save persists via PUT /api/materials/{id}/feedback-template (2.5s wait) and custom-rubric-badge-{material_id} appears; Restore-default clears textarea, Save persists empty, badge disappears; (10) MaterialLibrary: 2 edit-feedback-template-lib-{id} Sparkles buttons on homework rows open same EditFeedbackTemplateDialog (0 window.prompt hits confirmed); (11) REGRESSION pages /dashboard, /library, /submissions, /progress, /rubrics all load with 0 console errors and populated testid trees.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1770-1842 rubric endpoints do not enforce any name/content max length — an instructor could paste a 10 MB blob into `content` and persist it. Consider a soft cap (e.g., name <=200 chars, content <=8000 chars) with a 400 response, matching the existing feedback_template UX where the AI system prompt has a practical token budget.

RubricLibrary.js:89 uses window.confirm() for delete — same UX/Safari-compat concern that iteration_34/35 flagged for the OLD homework edit flow (which was correctly migrated to a Dialog in this iteration). For consistency, delete confirmation should be migrated to a shadcn AlertDialog too. Not a blocker; behavior currently works in Chromium.

FeedbackTemplateField.js:37-42 handles axios rejection with console.warn only and shows no user-visible fallback. If /api/rubrics returns 500 (say, mongo hiccup), the picker will silently show 'Rubric Library is empty' as if that were the true state. Consider adding a small inline error hint below the picker (or a subtle toast) so instructors know the library failed to load vs is actually empty.
RubricLibrary.js file (254 lines) + FeedbackTemplateField.js file (258 lines) are well under the 700-line threshold — no split needed. Component structure is clean and follows the existing pattern.

GET /api/rubrics streams up to 1000 rubrics with no pagination or filter. Fine for MVP org-wide sharing at ~current scale but will become an N+1 when the users table lookup runs inside the loop for each rubric with missing created_by_name (line 1777). Consider either: (a) backfilling created_by_name at write time only (already done in POST/PUT) and dropping the runtime backfill in GET, or (b) batching the user lookups. Currently harmless because all newly-created rubrics have created_by_name set.

The rubric picker inside FeedbackTemplateField auto-fetches /api/rubrics on every mount. In the cohort MaterialsTab, opening N EditFeedbackTemplateDialog instances (one per homework card) will fire N fetches. Consider lifting rubric list state to a React context or SWR-style cache to dedupe.
